passages.P5: In 1962, Nigeria conducted a population census that appeared to challenge the North’s established population majority. The results were rejected, and a second census followed in 1963. That exercise produced another controversy, this time reaching the Supreme Court. As Nigeria approached the 1964 federal election, disputes over population, parliamentary representation and political power intensified. Discover how the struggle over census figures became part of the wider crisis that preceded the collapse of Nigeria’s First Republic.
